headline: Spanish Common Grammar Patterns Master
threshold: Use sixty everyday structures, including tener que, hay que, ir a, acabar de and common clause patterns. Ordered for learning, not an asserted statistical frequency ranking.

lessons.title: Para + infinitive: purpose
lessons.objective: Para + infinitive: purpose: Para plus infinitive states a purpose with an understood subject shared with the main action.

words.es: Fui al mercado para comprar verduras.
words.en: I went to the market to buy vegetables.

words.es: Mi hermana llegó temprano para ayudarme.
words.en: My sister arrived early to help me.

words.es: Puse una nota en la puerta para recordar la hora.
words.en: I put a note on the door to remember the time.

words.es: Abrimos la ventana para enfriar la cocina.
words.en: We opened the window to cool the kitchen.

words.es: Llamé a los invitados para confirmar la dirección.
words.en: I called the guests to confirm the address.

words.es: Después guardé el teléfono para concentrarme en la cena.
words.en: Afterward I put my phone away to concentrate on dinner.

words.es: Este paquete es para mi hermana.
words.en: This package is for my sister.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing preparing a welcome dinner. Para plus infinitive states a purpose with an understood subject shared with the main action. A distinct subject commonly needs para que + subjunctive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Para plus infinitive states a purpose with an understood subject shared with the main action. A distinct subject commonly needs para que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Fui al mercado para comprar verduras.
examples.en: I went to the market to buy vegetables.

examples.es: Mi hermana llegó temprano para ayudarme.
examples.en: My sister arrived early to help me.

lessons.title: Para que + subjunctive: a new subject
lessons.objective: Para que + subjunctive: a new subject: Para que introduces a purpose clause and normally takes subjunctive.
lessons.focus: Para que + subjunctive: a new subject

words.es: Escribo despacio para que entiendas la dirección.
words.en: I write slowly so that you understand the address.

words.es: También separo los pasos para que todos puedan seguirlos.
words.en: I also separate the steps so that everyone can follow them.

words.es: Ana envía un mapa para que nadie se pierda.
words.en: Ana sends a map so that nobody gets lost.

words.es: Voy a llamar para que podamos confirmar la hora.
words.en: I am going to call so that we can confirm the time.

words.es: Dejé una copia para que la recepcionista tuviera los datos.
words.en: I left a copy so that the receptionist would have the details.

words.es: No quiero que un error pequeño cambie la visita.
words.en: I do not want a small mistake to change the visit.

words.es: Le escribí a Rosa esta mañana.
words.en: I wrote to Rosa this morning.

words.es: Le expliqué el cambio de horario.
words.en: I explained the schedule change to her.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing making a message easier to follow. Para que introduces a purpose clause and normally takes subjunctive. Its verb agrees with the subject of the purpose clause. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Para que introduces a purpose clause and normally takes subjunctive. Its verb agrees with the subject of the purpose clause.

examples.es: Escribo despacio para que entiendas la dirección.
examples.en: I write slowly so that you understand the address.

examples.es: También separo los pasos para que todos puedan seguirlos.
examples.en: I also separate the steps so that everyone can follow them.

lessons.title: Antes de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Antes de + infinitive: Antes de plus infinitive locates an action before another with an understood shared subject.

words.es: Antes de salir, reviso la mochila.
words.en: Before leaving, I check the backpack.

words.es: Mi hermano cierra las ventanas antes de bajar.
words.en: My brother closes the windows before going downstairs.

words.es: Antes de cerrar la puerta, buscamos las llaves.
words.en: Before closing the door, we look for the keys.

words.es: Voy a llamar al hotel antes de tomar el tren.
words.en: I am going to call the hotel before taking the train.

words.es: ¿Puedes revisar el horario antes de comprar los boletos?
words.en: Can you check the schedule before buying the tickets?

words.es: Así podremos corregir cualquier error a tiempo.
words.en: That way we will be able to correct any error in time.
Do you have the hotel reservation?

words.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
words.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a checklist before leaving home. Antes de plus infinitive locates an action before another with an understood shared subject. Retain de; do not conjugate the infinitive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Antes de plus infinitive locates an action before another with an understood shared subject. Retain de; do not conjugate the infinitive.

examples.es: Antes de salir, reviso la mochila.
examples.en: Before leaving, I check the backpack.

examples.es: Mi hermano cierra las ventanas antes de bajar.
examples.en: My brother closes the windows before going downstairs.

lessons.title: Antes de que + subjunctive
lessons.objective: Antes de que + subjunctive: Antes de que introduces a finite clause and normally takes subjunctive, including when the surrounding narrative is past.

words.es: Vamos a ordenar la sala antes de que lleguen.
words.en: We are going to tidy the living room before they arrive.

words.es: Ana quiere poner flores antes de que empiece la visita.
words.en: Ana wants to put out flowers before the visit begins.

words.es: Antes de que salga el tren, les mandaré la dirección.
words.en: Before the train leaves, I will send them the address.

words.es: Ayer limpiamos el patio antes de que oscureciera.
words.en: Yesterday we cleaned the courtyard before it got dark.

words.es: También compramos pan antes de que cerrara la tienda.
words.en: We also bought bread before the store closed.

words.es: Ahora solo falta confirmar cuántas personas vienen.
words.en: Now all that remains is to confirm how many people are coming.

words.es: Quiero que mis padres conozcan la ciudad.
words.en: I want my parents to get to know the city.

words.es: Espero que el viaje sea tranquilo.
words.en: I hope the trip is peaceful.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing getting a room ready for visitors. Antes de que introduces a finite clause and normally takes subjunctive, including when the surrounding narrative is past. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Antes de que introduces a finite clause and normally takes subjunctive, including when the surrounding narrative is past.

examples.es: Vamos a ordenar la sala antes de que lleguen.
examples.en: We are going to tidy the living room before they arrive.

examples.es: Ana quiere poner flores antes de que empiece la visita.
examples.en: Ana wants to put out flowers before the visit begins.

lessons.title: Después de + infinitive
lessons.objective: Después de + infinitive: Después de plus infinitive places an event after another activity.

words.es: Después de trabajar, camino hasta la estación.
words.en: After working, I walk to the station.

words.es: Mi compañera compra fruta después de salir de la oficina.
words.en: My coworker buys fruit after leaving the office.

words.es: Después de llegar a casa, preparo algo sencillo.
words.en: After getting home, I make something simple.

words.es: Llamo a mi familia después de cenar.
words.en: I call my family after dinner.

words.es: Después de hablar con ellos, leo unos minutos.
words.en: After talking to them, I read for a few minutes.

words.es: No miro mensajes del trabajo después de acostarme.
words.en: I do not look at work messages after going to bed.
I normally used to have breakfast at home.

words.es: El lunes desayuné en la estación.
words.en: On Monday I had breakfast at the station.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing an evening after a long workday. Después de plus infinitive places an event after another activity. The infinitive is not conjugated; a distinct subject may need después de que and a finite verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Después de plus infinitive places an event after another activity. The infinitive is not conjugated; a distinct subject may need después de que and a finite verb.

examples.es: Después de trabajar, camino hasta la estación.
examples.en: After working, I walk to the station.

examples.es: Mi compañera compra fruta después de salir de la oficina.
examples.en: My coworker buys fruit after leaving the office.

lessons.title: Cuando + subjunctive: pending event
lessons.objective: Cuando + subjunctive: pending event: Cuando with a future or pending event normally takes present subjunctive.

words.es: Cuando llegue el repartidor, revisaré la caja.
words.en: When the delivery driver arrives, I will check the box.

words.es: Cuando tengamos el recibo, te enviaré una foto.
words.en: When we have the receipt, I will send you a photo.

words.es: Mi hermana abrirá la puerta cuando suene el timbre.
words.en: My sister will open the door when the bell rings.

words.es: Cuando llega un paquete pequeño, el portero nos llama.
words.en: When a small package arrives, the doorman calls us.

words.es: Hoy no saldremos hasta que termine la entrega.
words.en: Today we will not leave until the delivery is finished.

words.es: Cuando estemos listos, podremos ir al mercado.
words.en: When we are ready, we will be able to go to the market.

words.es: Cuando llega un paquete, el portero nos llama.
words.en: When a package arrives, the doorman calls us.

words.es: Hoy estamos esperando una mesa nueva.
words.en: Today we are waiting for a new table.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing waiting to confirm a delivery. Cuando with a future or pending event normally takes present subjunctive. Habitual or established events take indicative; do not choose mood from cuando alone. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Cuando with a future or pending event normally takes present subjunctive. Habitual or established events take indicative; do not choose mood from cuando alone.

examples.es: Cuando llegue el repartidor, revisaré la caja.
examples.en: When the delivery driver arrives, I will check the box.

examples.es: Cuando tengamos el recibo, te enviaré una foto.
examples.en: When we have the receipt, I will send you a photo.

lessons.title: Si + present: open conditions
lessons.objective: Si + present: open conditions: For an open future condition use si + present indicative; the result may be future, present or a command.

words.es: Si hace buen tiempo, iremos al lago.
words.en: If the weather is good, we will go to the lake.
If it rains, we will visit the museum.
If you have a camera, bring it.

words.es: Podemos invitar a Ana si está libre.
words.en: We can invite Ana if she is free.

words.es: Si vienen más personas, compraremos más comida.
words.en: If more people come, we will buy more food.

words.es: Te llamaré si hay algún cambio.
words.en: I will call you if there is any change.

words.es: Si hace buen tiempo, iremos al parque.
words.en: If the weather is good, we will go to the park.
If it rains, we will eat at home.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a flexible weekend plan. For an open future condition use si + present indicative; the result may be future, present or a command. Do not put the future directly after conditional si. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: For an open future condition use si + present indicative; the result may be future, present or a command. Do not put the future directly after conditional si.

examples.es: Si hace buen tiempo, iremos al lago.
examples.en: If the weather is good, we will go to the lake.

examples.es: Si llueve, visitaremos el museo.
examples.en: If it rains, we will visit the museum.

lessons.title: Si + imperfect subjunctive: hypotheses
lessons.objective: Si + imperfect subjunctive: hypotheses: Use si + imperfect subjunctive for a hypothetical condition and conditional for its result.

words.es: Si tuviera una tarde libre, iría a la biblioteca.
words.en: If I had a free afternoon, I would go to the library.

words.es: Mi hermana vendría si no trabajara.
words.en: My sister would come if she did not work.

words.es: Si pudiéramos elegir, estudiaríamos por la mañana.
words.en: If we could choose, we would study in the morning.
What would you do if you lived closer?

words.es: Yo caminaría al centro todos los días.
words.en: I would walk downtown every day.

words.es: Si organizáramos mejor las tareas, tendríamos más tiempo.
words.en: If we organized the tasks better, we would have more time.

words.es: Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería a tocar el piano.
words.en: If I had more time, I would learn to play the piano.

words.es: Si viviera cerca, iría a clase a pie.
words.en: If I lived nearby, I would walk to class.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing imagining a quieter week. Use si + imperfect subjunctive for a hypothetical condition and conditional for its result. This course practices the -ra alternative. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use si + imperfect subjunctive for a hypothetical condition and conditional for its result. This course practices the -ra alternative.

examples.es: Si tuviera una tarde libre, iría a la biblioteca.
examples.en: If I had a free afternoon, I would go to the library.

examples.es: Mi hermana vendría si no trabajara.
examples.en: My sister would come if she did not work.

lessons.title: Aunque + indicative: accepted facts
lessons.objective: Aunque + indicative: accepted facts: Aunque with indicative can concede information presented as a fact.

words.es: Aunque el curso es corto, exige práctica diaria.
words.en: Although the course is short, it requires daily practice.

words.es: Me inscribí aunque trabajo por la mañana.
words.en: I enrolled although I work in the morning.

words.es: Aunque la escuela queda lejos, puedo llegar en autobús.
words.en: Although the school is far away, I can get there by bus.

words.es: El precio me parece justo aunque no incluye el libro.
words.en: The price seems fair to me although it does not include the book.

words.es: Aunque estaba cansado, fui a la primera clase.
words.en: Although I was tired, I went to the first class.

words.es: Ahora quiero mantener un horario realista.
words.en: Now I want to maintain a realistic schedule.

words.es: El curso es corto; sin embargo, exige práctica diaria.
words.en: The course is short; however, it requires daily practice.

words.es: Aunque trabajo por la mañana, puedo asistir por la tarde.
words.en: Although I work in the morning, I can attend in the afternoon.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explaining a course choice. Aunque with indicative can concede information presented as a fact. It means although in these examples; the rest of the sentence gives the contrasting point. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Aunque with indicative can concede information presented as a fact. It means although in these examples; the rest of the sentence gives the contrasting point.

examples.es: Aunque el curso es corto, exige práctica diaria.
examples.en: Although the course is short, it requires daily practice.

examples.es: Me inscribí aunque trabajo por la mañana.
examples.en: I enrolled although I work in the morning.

lessons.title: Aunque + subjunctive: even if
lessons.objective: Aunque + subjunctive: even if: Aunque with subjunctive can present a condition as hypothetical or as irrelevant to the result.

words.es: Voy a practicar aunque tenga poco tiempo.
words.en: I am going to practice even if I have little time.

words.es: Aunque llueva, iré a la biblioteca.
words.en: Even if it rains, I will go to the library.

words.es: Mi compañero vendrá aunque salga tarde del trabajo.
words.en: My classmate will come even if he leaves work late.

words.es: Aunque el ejercicio parezca fácil, conviene revisarlo.
words.en: Even if the exercise seems easy, it is advisable to review it.

words.es: No voy a cambiar de plan aunque mis amigos prefieran salir.
words.en: I am not going to change my plan even if my friends prefer to go out.
We will be able to see each other after studying.

words.es: El curso es corto; sin embargo, exige práctica diaria.
words.en: The course is short; however, it requires daily practice.

words.es: Aunque trabajo por la mañana, puedo asistir por la tarde.
words.en: Although I work in the morning, I can attend in the afternoon.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing keeping a study commitment. Aunque with subjunctive can present a condition as hypothetical or as irrelevant to the result. It is not simply a mechanical marker of factual uncertainty. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Aunque with subjunctive can present a condition as hypothetical or as irrelevant to the result. It is not simply a mechanical marker of factual uncertainty.

examples.es: Voy a practicar aunque tenga poco tiempo.
examples.en: I am going to practice even if I have little time.

examples.es: Aunque llueva, iré a la biblioteca.
examples.en: Even if it rains, I will go to the library.

lessons.title: Por eso: consequence
lessons.objective: Por eso: consequence: Por eso connects an already stated cause to its consequence.

words.es: El autobús llegó tarde; por eso perdí la cita.
words.en: The bus arrived late; that is why I missed the appointment.

words.es: No había otro servicio, por eso tuve que caminar.
words.en: There was no other service, so I had to walk.

words.es: Llegué cansado porque había caminado mucho.
words.en: I arrived tired because I had walked a lot.

words.es: La recepcionista tenía mi número, por eso pudo llamarme.
words.en: The receptionist had my number, so she was able to call me.

words.es: Me ofreció otra hora porque alguien había cancelado.
words.en: She offered me another time because someone had canceled.

words.es: Por eso pude resolver el problema ese mismo día.
words.en: That is why I was able to solve the problem that same day.

words.es: Tuve una cita en el centro.
El autobús estuvo lleno toda la mañana.
words.en: The bus was full all morning.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explaining a missed appointment. Por eso connects an already stated cause to its consequence. Porque normally introduces the cause itself; practice both directions without treating them as interchangeable. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Por eso connects an already stated cause to its consequence. Porque normally introduces the cause itself; practice both directions without treating them as interchangeable.

examples.es: El autobús llegó tarde; por eso perdí la cita.
examples.en: The bus arrived late; that is why I missed the appointment.

examples.es: No había otro servicio, por eso tuve que caminar.
examples.en: There was no other service, so I had to walk.

lessons.title: A pesar de + noun / infinitive
lessons.objective: A pesar de + noun / infinitive: A pesar de introduces a concession before a noun or infinitive.

words.es: A pesar de la lluvia, llegamos a tiempo.
words.en: Despite the rain, we arrived on time.

words.es: Mi hermana fue a clase a pesar de estar cansada.
words.en: My sister went to class despite being tired.

words.es: A pesar de tener poco espacio, organizamos bien la sala.
words.en: Despite having little space, we organized the room well.

words.es: El grupo terminó el proyecto a pesar de los cambios.
words.en: The group finished the project despite the changes.

words.es: A pesar de que faltaban dos personas, pudimos reunirnos.
words.en: Although two people were missing, we were able to meet.
Afterward we agreed to send them a summary.

words.es: Primero hablemos de la fecha de entrega.
words.en: First let us talk about the deadline.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing continuing despite a difficult day. A pesar de introduces a concession before a noun or infinitive. A finite clause normally uses a pesar de que; do not drop de. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: A pesar de introduces a concession before a noun or infinitive. A finite clause normally uses a pesar de que; do not drop de.

examples.es: A pesar de la lluvia, llegamos a tiempo.
examples.en: Despite the rain, we arrived on time.

examples.es: Mi hermana fue a clase a pesar de estar cansada.
examples.en: My sister went to class despite being tired.

lessons.title: En vez de + infinitive
lessons.objective: En vez de + infinitive: En vez de + infinitive substitutes one action for another.

words.es: En vez de copiar todo, voy a escribir un resumen.
words.en: Instead of copying everything, I am going to write a summary.

words.es: Mi compañero decidió llamar en vez de enviar otro mensaje.
words.en: My classmate decided to call instead of sending another message.

words.es: En vez de trabajar solos, podemos revisar en parejas.
words.en: Instead of working alone, we can review in pairs.

words.es: Hoy caminamos en vez de tomar el autobús.
words.en: Today we walked instead of taking the bus.

words.es: No quiero adivinar en vez de preguntar.
words.en: I do not want to guess instead of asking.

words.es: Así sabremos qué información falta de verdad.
words.en: That way we will know what information is really missing.

words.es: Primero hablemos de la fecha de entrega.
words.en: First let us talk about the deadline.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing changing an inefficient routine. En vez de + infinitive substitutes one action for another. The alternative can also be a noun; retain de before the infinitive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: En vez de + infinitive substitutes one action for another. The alternative can also be a noun; retain de before the infinitive.

examples.es: En vez de copiar todo, voy a escribir un resumen.
examples.en: Instead of copying everything, I am going to write a summary.

examples.es: Mi compañero decidió llamar en vez de enviar otro mensaje.
examples.en: My classmate decided to call instead of sending another message.

lessons.title: Sin + infinitive
lessons.objective: Sin + infinitive: Sin plus infinitive describes an action not performed; the infinitive stays unchanged.

words.es: Envié el mensaje sin revisar la fecha.
words.en: I sent the message without checking the date.

words.es: Mi compañero salió sin llevar la carpeta.
words.en: My coworker left without taking the folder.

words.es: No podemos empezar sin confirmar los nombres.
words.en: We cannot begin without confirming the names.

words.es: Ana encontró la solución sin pedir ayuda.
words.en: Ana found the solution without asking for help.

words.es: Quiero explicar el error sin culpar a nadie.
words.en: I want to explain the error without blaming anyone.

words.es: La próxima vez revisaremos la lista antes de salir.
words.en: Next time we will check the list before leaving.

words.es: Le escribí a Rosa esta mañana.
words.en: I wrote to Rosa this morning.

words.es: Le expliqué el cambio de horario.
words.en: I explained the schedule change to her.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing a problem with an unfinished message. Sin plus infinitive describes an action not performed; the infinitive stays unchanged. A distinct subject can be introduced with sin que + subjunctive. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Sin plus infinitive describes an action not performed; the infinitive stays unchanged. A distinct subject can be introduced with sin que + subjunctive.

examples.es: Envié el mensaje sin revisar la fecha.
examples.en: I sent the message without checking the date.

examples.es: Mi compañero salió sin llevar la carpeta.
examples.en: My coworker left without taking the folder.

lessons.title: Al + infinitive: on doing something
lessons.objective: Al + infinitive: on doing something: Al plus infinitive commonly introduces an action coinciding with or immediately preceding the main event: al llegar.

words.es: Al llegar a la oficina, vi una nota en la puerta.
words.en: On arriving at the office, I saw a note on the door.

words.es: Al leerla, entendí por qué no había nadie.
words.en: On reading it, I understood why nobody was there.

words.es: Mi compañera me llamó al salir de la reunión.
words.en: My coworker called me when leaving the meeting.

words.es: Al revisar el mensaje, encontramos la dirección nueva.
words.en: On checking the message, we found the new address.

words.es: Al no tener coche, tuvimos que tomar un taxi.
words.en: Since we did not have a car, we had to take a taxi.

words.es: Al final llegamos antes de que terminara la reunión.
words.en: In the end we arrived before the meeting finished.

words.es: No hay nadie en la oficina.
words.en: There is nobody in the office.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing noticing a mistake on arrival. Al plus infinitive commonly introduces an action coinciding with or immediately preceding the main event: al llegar. It can also express cause in context. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Al plus infinitive commonly introduces an action coinciding with or immediately preceding the main event: al llegar. It can also express cause in context.

examples.es: Al llegar a la oficina, vi una nota en la puerta.
examples.en: On arriving at the office, I saw a note on the door.

examples.es: Al leerla, entendí por qué no había nadie.
examples.en: On reading it, I understood why nobody was there.

lessons.title: Tan ... como: equality
lessons.objective: Tan ... como: equality: Tan modifies an adjective or adverb before como; tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas quantify nouns and agree with them.

words.es: Esta sala es tan tranquila como la biblioteca.
words.en: This room is as quiet as the library.

words.es: Las mesas no son tan grandes como las del piso de arriba.
words.en: The tables are not as large as those upstairs.

words.es: Aquí puedo leer tan bien como en casa.
words.en: Here I can read as well as at home.

words.es: No hay tantas sillas como necesitamos.
words.en: There are not as many chairs as we need.

words.es: Mi amiga estudia tanto como yo.
words.en: My friend studies as much as I do.

words.es: Elegiremos el lugar que tenga espacio para todos.
words.en: We will choose the place that has space for everyone.

words.es: Este apartamento es más luminoso que el otro.
words.en: This apartment is brighter than the other one.

words.es: La cocina es menos grande, pero está mejor equipada.
words.en: The kitchen is smaller, but it is better equipped.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing comparing two study spaces. Tan modifies an adjective or adverb before como; tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas quantify nouns and agree with them. Tanto como can compare amounts of action. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Tan modifies an adjective or adverb before como; tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas quantify nouns and agree with them. Tanto como can compare amounts of action.

examples.es: Esta sala es tan tranquila como la biblioteca.
examples.en: This room is as quiet as the library.

examples.es: Las mesas no son tan grandes como las del piso de arriba.
examples.en: The tables are not as large as those upstairs.

lessons.title: Más ... que: comparison
lessons.objective: Más ... que: comparison: Más / menos plus adjective, adverb or noun compares with que.

words.es: Esta ruta es más corta que la otra.
words.en: This route is shorter than the other one.

words.es: El autobús pasa menos veces que el tren.
words.en: The bus runs fewer times than the train.

words.es: Caminar es más tranquilo que conducir con tráfico.
words.en: Walking is more peaceful than driving in traffic.

words.es: El tren tarda menos de veinte minutos.
words.en: The train takes less than twenty minutes.

words.es: Hoy la primera opción parece mejor que ayer.
words.en: Today the first option seems better than yesterday.

words.es: Voy a probar las dos antes de decidir.
words.en: I am going to try both before deciding.

words.es: Este apartamento es más luminoso que el otro.
words.en: This apartment is brighter than the other one.

words.es: La cocina es menos grande, pero está mejor equipada.
words.en: The kitchen is smaller, but it is better equipped.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing choosing a route to class. Más / menos plus adjective, adverb or noun compares with que. Mejor and peor often replace más bueno and más malo. Before a numerical threshold, use de in many contexts. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Más / menos plus adjective, adverb or noun compares with que. Mejor and peor often replace más bueno and más malo. Before a numerical threshold, use de in many contexts.

examples.es: Esta ruta es más corta que la otra.
examples.en: This route is shorter than the other one.

examples.es: El autobús pasa menos veces que el tren.
examples.en: The bus runs fewer times than the train.

lessons.title: Se puede + infinitive: general possibility
lessons.objective: Se puede + infinitive: general possibility: Se puede expresses a general possibility or permission followed by an infinitive.

words.es: Aquí se puede estudiar hasta las ocho.
words.en: Here one can study until eight.

words.es: ¿Se puede usar la sala sin reservar?
words.en: Can one use the room without booking?

words.es: No se puede comer junto a las computadoras.
words.en: One cannot eat next to the computers.

words.es: Se puede pedir ayuda en la recepción.
words.en: One can ask for help at reception.

words.es: Antes no se podía entrar los sábados.
words.en: Previously one could not enter on Saturdays.

words.es: Ahora se puede venir también por la mañana.
words.en: Now one can also come in the morning.

words.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
Deje la mochila en el casillero.
words.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing finding out how a center works. Se puede expresses a general possibility or permission followed by an infinitive. Context may instead support a passive reading with agreement; this lesson practices the impersonal construction. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Se puede expresses a general possibility or permission followed by an infinitive. Context may instead support a passive reading with agreement; this lesson practices the impersonal construction.

examples.es: Aquí se puede estudiar hasta las ocho.
examples.en: Here one can study until eight.

examples.es: ¿Se puede usar la sala sin reservar?
examples.en: Can one use the room without booking?

lessons.title: Soler + infinitive: usual habits
lessons.objective: Soler + infinitive: usual habits: Soler + infinitive describes what someone usually does.

words.es: Suelo leer un poco antes de desayunar.
words.en: I usually read a little before breakfast.

words.es: Mi hermana suele escuchar las noticias.
words.en: My sister usually listens to the news.
Where do you usually study in the afternoon?
We usually meet at the library.
I used to study at night.

words.es: Ahora prefiero practicar cuando estoy más descansado.
words.en: Now I prefer to practice when I am better rested.
We used to live near the river.

words.es: Nuestra casa tenía un patio pequeño.
words.en: Our house had a small courtyard.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describing ordinary study habits. Soler + infinitive describes what someone usually does. Present suelo / sueles changes o to ue; nosotros solemos keeps o. Imperfect solía describes a former habit. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Soler + infinitive describes what someone usually does. Present suelo / sueles changes o to ue; nosotros solemos keeps o. Imperfect solía describes a former habit.

examples.es: Suelo leer un poco antes de desayunar.
examples.en: I usually read a little before breakfast.

examples.es: Mi hermana suele escuchar las noticias.
examples.en: My sister usually listens to the news.

lessons.title: Haber + participle: completed actions
lessons.objective: Haber + participle: completed actions: Conjugate auxiliary haber and keep the participle invariant.

words.en: We have already prepared the room.

words.es: Ana ha escrito el resumen del proyecto.
words.en: Ana has written the project summary.

words.es: Todavía no he abierto el mensaje del director.
words.en: I have not opened the director's message yet.

words.es: Cuando llegó, ya habíamos puesto las carpetas en la mesa.
words.en: When he arrived, we had already put the folders on the table.

words.es: Él nos dijo que había leído la primera versión.
words.en: He told us that he had read the first version.

words.es: Ahora podemos comprobar juntos los últimos cambios.
words.en: Now we can check the latest changes together.

words.es: He abierto la sala de reuniones.
words.en: I have opened the meeting room.

words.es: Ana ha puesto las carpetas sobre la mesa.
words.en: Ana has put the folders on the table.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing reviewing what the team has finished. Conjugate auxiliary haber and keep the participle invariant. He escrito and había escrito locate completion at different reference points; do not replace haber with tener. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Conjugate auxiliary haber and keep the participle invariant. He escrito and había escrito locate completion at different reference points; do not replace haber with tener.

examples.es: Ya hemos preparado la sala.
examples.en: We have already prepared the room.

examples.es: Ana ha escrito el resumen del proyecto.
examples.en: Ana has written the project summary.
